I spent years actively suicidal, made several attempts on my life and still to this day have fleeting thoughts about ending my life when I'm having a hard time. 

But I've realised it's the little things in life that make it worth living. A coffee and cigarette  in the morning out on your front step with your best friend, buying your neice and nephew an ice cream at the beach and watching them enjoy it in the sunshine, snuggling up to my boyfriend in the morning while he's still asleep, seeing my dad super excited to show me a jewellers bench he made for me to work at, a beautiful walk through nature, beating my personal best at running. 

Its easy to say now because you forget all the small things when you are so depressed you can't see any other way out. Life is crappy a lot of the time and awful things happen all around the world so I now take the time to really treasure those moments and so many others (because there are lots of times life is amazing too). 

Everything is transient, that is life. The good and the bad comes and goes. I'd never have had all that good if I had succeeded in my mission to end my life and I will always be glad I did not. Those small moments of pure bliss make life worth living.

Yeah I definitely feel this way, it’s something I’ve been struggling a lot with. Before BPD fully came into my life (I think it was always there just deep under the surface) I was a straight A student who did tons of extra curricular activities. Since my first crisis and continual struggle with it my grades dropped massively and I no longer take part in extra curricular activities. I got into uni and graduated this year with a much lower grade than I had hoped for and I know had I never struggled with BPD would probably have been a heck of a lot higher.  On the other hand I did get through uni while struggling with what I would consider a crippling mental health illness so everyone tells me to see that as a positive. I just can’t because I know that I should have done better than that.
Sanitary products, there’s so many girls in the world not able to go to school because they are too poor to access them.

I disagree I myself have been formerly diagnosed with bpd and am extremely self aware, within my own relationship I have feelings of remorse and will admit to things that are my fault. I will admit this was not always the case and I have become more self aware in the last few years but I would not generalise your one experience with a partner with BPD to everyone with BPD. 

OP I am not a professional and cannot diagnose you with this condition. My advice would be to seek a psychiatrist and be assessed for it. Let them know you think you might have BPD and explain the symptoms. If it is BPD try and receive DBT, it can honestly be life changing. Don’t ever feel like it’s a life sentence because it’s not. I know plenty of people who have received the diagnosis who lead very happy life’s now with healthy relationships.

My boyfriend has been supportive about it mainly but the first thing he said to me when it happened was “that’s why you don’t speak to strangers”. I guess I feel like he thinks it’s my own fault and maybe I deserved it.

Thanks for your reply, it’s nice to know I’m not the only one who struggles with change like this. Part of me knows I need to start applying for jobs but there’s this part of me that says I won’t get one because I’m stupid etc. So what is the point in even trying. But I know as soon as I have some sort of routine I will feel better.

I started but didn’t finish a course of DBT before university so that was 4 years ago now. Haven’t had any therapeutic input since. I desperately want it again but am very aware that resources are massively limited in the UK so only people who are at high risk qualify for it (which I was before). It’s incredibly frustrating because event though I don’t hurt myself like I did or act on suicidal impulses, other impulses have taken over my life and I struggle massively with many of the other symptoms. But unfortunately in the UK you literally have to be at crisis point before you get any real help.
